![RICE Framework: How to Use RICE for Project Prioritization](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/10081544-2633-0066-0000-cb13f19e5d0e:4)
The RICE framework is `a data-driven scoring model used by product teams to rank projects, features, and ideas objectively`.[[1]](https://www.productplan.com/glossary/rice-scoring-model)[[2]](https://skillifysolutions.com/blogs/safe/rice-method-prioritization/)

### The RICE Formula

The RICE score uses a simple mathematical calculation to weigh value against the cost of implementation:[[1]](https://faridjafarzade.medium.com/rice-matrix-a-practical-prioritization-framework-for-product-owners-and-product-managers-2b71dccd0a08)[[2]](https://skillifysolutions.com/blogs/safe/rice-method-prioritization/)  
RICE Score=Reach×Impact×Confidence Effort RICE Score equals the fraction with numerator Reach cross Impact cross Confidence and denominator Effort end-fraction R I C E S c o r e=R e a c h×I m p a c t×C o n f i d e n c e E f f o r t

### The Four Components

- **Reach:** The number of users or customers an initiative affects within a specific time period, such as users per month or transactions per quarter.
- **Impact:** How much an initiative will increase user value or conversion, usually measured on a scale from 0.5 (minimal) to 3.0 (massive).
- **Confidence:** A percentage (typically 50% to 100%) showing how certain you are about your estimates for reach, impact, and effort.
- **Effort:** The total time and resources required by the team, measured in person-months or person-weeks.[[1]](https://www.intercom.com/blog/rice-simple-prioritization-for-product-managers/)[[2]](https://faridjafarzade.medium.com/rice-matrix-a-practical-prioritization-framework-for-product-owners-and-product-managers-2b71dccd0a08)[[3]](https://www.notion.com/blog/rice-prioritization)[[4]](https://www.productboard.com/glossary/product-prioritization-frameworks/)[[5]](https://productschool.com/blog/product-fundamentals/rice-framework)[[6]](https://agileseekers.com/blog/feature-prioritization-using-rice-and-ice-models-in-product-roadmaps)[[7]](https://www.avion.io/blog/rice-prioritization/)

Learn more about managing roadmaps with the [ProductPlan Glossary](https://www.productplan.com/glossary/rice-scoring-model) or review broader [Atlassian Prioritization Frameworks](https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/prioritization-framework).If you want, I can help you:

- Walk through a **practical scoring example** with two competing project ideas.
- Compare RICE with alternative methods like **ICE or MoSCoW**.
